content.text: Preferans (derived from the French 'PrÃ©fÃ©rence') is the quintessential card game of the Russian intelligentsia and one of the most intellectually demanding games in existence. Played by 3 or 4 players with a 32-card deck, it is a bidding-based trick-taking game where players compete for contracts, including the dreaded 'Misere' (taking zero tricks). It is famous for its complex 'Pula' (pool) scoring system involving 'Bullets', 'Whists', and 'Mountains', making it a game of long-term strategy and cold mathematical calculation.
Developed in Russia in the mid-19th century from French games like 'L'Hombre' and 'Boston'. It became the preferred game of the Russian military, students, and nobility.
Typically 3 active players. If 4, the dealer sits out and gets 'Buy-in' points.
2 cards each, 2 to the 'Talon' (the Widow), continuing until everyone has 10 cards.

items.text: Sochi scoring: Pool, whist and dump points; declarer and defenders score or pay per contract and tricks.
Rostov (Moscow) scoring: Dump penalties for whisters halved; dump points replaced by 5 whist points per point to each opponent.

Misère and all-pass: Misère: bid to take zero tricks; ranks between 8 NT and 9 spades; played at no trumps with defenders' cards face up. All-pass (raspasovka): when no one bids, each player tries to take as few tricks as possible; no trumps.
